$comment: Researched 2026-07-28 against official Meta docs. `verified: true` means read verbatim from a Meta doc page. Meta renamed the Marketing API tiers in May 2026 and ships a new Marketing API version roughly every four months on a 90-day deprecation clock, so re-check versions and tier names before relying on them.

policy.graph: Each version lives at least 2 years. Unversioned calls fall back to the version set in App Dashboard > Settings > Advanced.
policy.marketing: Only ~90 days of overlap after a new version ships, and releases land about every four months. Marketing API does NOT support unversioned calls — omit the version and the call fails.
policy.warning_header: X-Ad-Api-Version-Warning tells you an auto-upgrade fired.

system_user_non_expiring.caution: Meta now states some businesses MUST use expiring tokens, and that omitting the expiry parameter errors for them. Treat non-expiring as deprecated in practice; design for the 60-day path anyway.

system_user_60_day.lifetime: 60 days from generation or last refresh
system_user_60_day.note: Refresh returns a NEW token string that replaces the old one. The old token stays valid until its original expiry, giving a zero-downtime overlap window. Revoke the old one explicitly after deploying the new one.

user_long_lived.note: Server-side only, needs the app secret. An expired token cannot be exchanged. Do not reuse one long-lived token across multiple clients.

page_long_lived.obtain: GET /{app-scoped-user-id}/accounts using a long-lived user token
page_long_lived.note: Unique per Page + admin + app combination. Dies with error 190 subcode 492 if the user loses their Page role.

app.lifetime: Until the app secret is reset
app.note: Server-to-server only. Rejected entirely if the app type is Native/Desktop.

marketing-api.label: Marketing API (campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives)
quirks: Marketing API refuses unversioned calls. Always pin a version in the path.
Everything should be created PAUSED and activated deliberately; both the Ads CLI and the hosted MCP server do this by default.
Budgets are in minor units — 5000 means $50.00.
Creation order is campaign, then ad set, then creative, then ad. An ad references a creative that must already exist.
Lifetime budget requires an end time. Omit ad set budget entirely when the campaign uses campaign budget optimisation.

ads-insights.label: Ads Insights (reporting)
quirks: Has its own throttle header, X-FB-Ads-Insights-Throttle, separate from the BUC header.
Async report jobs exist for heavy queries; sync calls with wide date ranges and many breakdowns hit complexity_score limits.
Remedy for a complexity throttle is shorter time ranges, fewer object ids, fewer metrics or fewer breakdowns.

conversions-api.label: Conversions API (server-side events)
quirks: ads_read is the CAPI permission — it grants server-side event access, which surprises people who assume ads_management.
The dataset id IS the pixel id; Meta renamed pixels to datasets and the ids are interchangeable.
A dataset-scoped token generated in Events Manager avoids needing an app at all for pure CAPI work.
test_event_code routes events to the Test Events tool instead of production. Never leave it set in production.
Send events within an hour where possible; user data fields must be SHA-256 hashed except when Meta specifies otherwise.

business-management.label: Business Management API (businesses, ad accounts, system users, asset assignment)
quirks: This is what IS automatable on Meta: creating businesses, ad accounts, system users, assigning assets, minting tokens.
It cannot create an app. POST /{business_id}/owned_apps claims an existing app and takes no parameters.
Limited (formerly Standard) Marketing API tier gives no Business Manager access for managing ad accounts, users or Pages.

catalog.label: Catalog / Commerce
quirks: catalog_management depends on business_management — requesting it alone fails.
Catalog Batch has its own BUC error code, 80014, separate from Catalog Management's 80009.
Catalogs with active feeds or referencing ads cannot be deleted.

custom-audiences.label: Custom Audiences
quirks: User identifiers must be SHA-256 hashed and normalised before upload.
Has its own BUC bucket, so audience uploads do not consume ads_management quota.

instagram.label: Instagram (business accounts, media, boosting)
quirks: instagram_basic depends on pages_read_user_content and pages_show_list.
System user tokens do not carry the newer instagram_business_* permissions — check the supported scope list before assuming.

whatsapp.label: WhatsApp Business
quirks: Requires a business portfolio.
Own BUC bucket with error code 80008.

pages.label: Pages
quirks: Neither Marketing API tier can create Pages through the API.
Page throttling uses error 80001 with a Page or system user token, but error 32 with a user token.
A Page only appears to a system user if it was explicitly assigned to that system user.

leadgen.label: Lead Ads
quirks: Leads are only retrievable for 90 days.
Realtime delivery is via webhooks, not polling.

ads_management.does: read and manage ad accounts, create campaigns, manage ads, fetch metrics

ads_read.does: Ads Insights API reporting AND server-side Conversions API access

business_management.does: read and write the Business Manager API, manage and claim assets

catalog_management.does: create, read, update, delete business-owned product catalogs

pages_read_engagement.does: required by both Marketing API use cases and by ads_management

pages_show_list.does: list the Pages a user manages

pages_manage_ads.does: manage ads associated with a Page

read_insights.does: read insights; the Ads CLI asks for this rather than ads_read

instagram_basic.does: read an Instagram business profile and its media

whatsapp_business_management.does: manage WhatsApp business assets, numbers, templates, webhooks

ads_mcp_management.does: required by the hosted Ads MCP server only; no CLI or raw-API equivalent

graph_api_levels.standard: Automatic for all Business/Consumer/Gaming apps. Permissions can only be requested from users who have a ROLE ON YOUR APP. Enough for a single-tenant Worker managing your own assets.
graph_api_levels.advanced: Required to request permissions from anyone without a role on your app. Needs App Review AND Business Verification, plus annual Data Use Checkup.

marketing_api_tier.limited: Formerly 'Standard Access'. Automatic when you add the Marketing API product. Heavily rate limited per ad account, explicitly 'for development only, not for production apps running for live advertisers'. No Business Manager access to manage ad accounts, users or Pages. 1 system user + 1 admin system user.
marketing_api_tier.full: Formerly 'Advanced Access'. Lightly rate limited. Full Business Manager and Catalog API access. 10 system users + 1 admin system user.
marketing_api_tier.qualify: At least 500 Marketing API calls in the last 15 days (reduced from 1500 in May 2026) AND an error rate under 15% across the last 500 calls. These are maintenance requirements, not just entry requirements.
marketing_api_tier.chicken_and_egg: You must make 500 real calls while heavily rate limited before you can qualify for the lighter limits. Budget a warm-up period.

X-Business-Use-Case-Usage.shape: { business-object-id: [ { type, call_count, total_cputime, total_time, estimated_time_to_regain_access, ads_api_access_tier } ] }
X-Business-Use-Case-Usage.units: call_count, total_cputime and total_time are PERCENTAGES of the allowance over a rolling hour, not counts. estimated_time_to_regain_access is in MINUTES.

X-App-Usage.units: percentages over a rolling hour, app-wide

X-Ad-Account-Usage.units: reset_time_duration is in SECONDS — note the mismatch with the BUC header's minutes

error_codes.17: User-level too many calls; subcode 2446079 is the ad-account API-level limit
error_codes.32: Page request limit using a USER token
error_codes.613: Custom rate limit. Subcodes: 1487742 ad-account calls, 1487632 ad-set budget changes capped at 4/hour, 1487225 ad-creation daily spend cap, 5044001 100 QPS mutation burst, 1996 inconsistent request volume, null abuse-prevention throttle
error_codes.80001: Page calls with a Page or SYSTEM USER token
error_codes.80004: Ads Management BUC limit (subcode 2446079) — the one you will hit most

auth_errors.190: Token expired, revoked or invalid. Get a new one.
auth_errors.190.458: App Not Installed — the user has not authorised your app, or revoked it.
auth_errors.190.459: User Checkpointed — they must log in at facebook.com to clear an issue.
auth_errors.190.460: Password Changed, or the user logged out. Both produce this.
auth_errors.190.463: Expired — session expired on a given date.
auth_errors.190.467: Invalid Access Token — revoked or malformed.
auth_errors.190.492: Invalid Session — the user behind a Page token no longer has the right Page role. The classic Page-token killer.
auth_errors.100: Invalid parameter. The most common error overall.
auth_errors.104: Incorrect signature — appsecret_proof missing or wrong.
auth_errors.368: Action deemed abusive. Back off and retry later.
auth_errors.critical: Meta will NOT notify you that a token became invalid. You only find out on the next call. Tokens can also be invalidated early for security reasons with no signal at all.

ads-cli.label: Meta Ads CLI
ads-cli.form: Local Python package, pip install meta-ads, Python 3.12+, entrypoint `meta`
ads-cli.auth: System user access token only. No interactive login.
ads-cli.env_note: No META_ prefix. The variable really is just ACCESS_TOKEN.
quirks: Global flags must come BEFORE the subcommand: meta --output json ads campaign list.
Everything is created PAUSED. Going live takes three separate updates: campaign, ad set, ad.
Budgets in cents.
Business id resolution falls back to an interactive prompt, which hangs in CI. Set BUSINESS_ID explicitly.
Dataset creation is gated on a business admin accepting the business tools ToS — another interactive blocker.
Config precedence: CLI flags, then env vars, then project .env, then ~/.config/meta/.
The overview page advertises product-item and product-set commands that do not exist in the command reference. Verify with meta ads --help.

ads-mcp.label: Meta hosted Ads MCP server
ads-mcp.auth: OAuth via Facebook Login for Business, OR a USER access token in an Authorization: Bearer header
ads-mcp.connect_claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http --client-id <META_APP_ID> meta-ads https://mcp.facebook.com/ads
ads-mcp.tools: ~91 tools named ads_*, across reporting, ad management, catalogs, datasets, help, experiments and activity logs
quirks: Owning a Meta app is optional — there is a no-app route through Business Manager.
Uses USER tokens, not system user tokens. A token minted for the Ads CLI will not cleanly serve the MCP server and vice versa.
ads_mcp_management is MCP-only and has no CLI or raw-API equivalent.
Advanced Access on ads_mcp_management is required to manage other businesses' data as an agency.
Tool availability is rolling out gradually per ad account. Enumerate with tools/list rather than assuming.
The served tool list already runs ahead of the published docs.
Write tools create entities paused and ask for confirmation before activation.
